newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Europeans take to air to monitor Albania voting.
newsitem.headline: Europeans take to air to monitor Albania voting.

text.p: European officials who will ultimately judge the standard of Albania's general election made a whistle-stop helicopter tour of the country on Sunday for a first-hand assessment of the voting.

Escorted by an attack helicopter, the officials of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) and the Council of Europe boarded two big Huey transport helicopters to sweep north and south in the mountainous Balkan state to speak to international monitors and Albanian poll organisers.
The helicopters carried air gunners of the Italian Capricorno squadron stationed in Tirana, who scanned towns and villages as the aircraft swooped low.
Tension appeared greatest in the central towns of Lushnje and Berat. One OSCE official said observers in Lushnje had been told to leave the town by Monday morning.

"Observers have been well treated but they have advised to leave the area by tomorrow," OSCE official Christina Danielson of Sweden said at a Berat polling station. "Most people voted in the morning because they are too scared to go in the afternoon."
"The (Lushnje) observers are leaving tonight. The situation is too insecure there," another OSCE monitor said.

OSCE election certification officer Catherine Lalumiere and the leaders of delegations of the OSCE and Council of Europe parliamentary assemblies, witnessed a ballot box being opened in Berat by members of the electoral commission, which included both a Socialist and a member of President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party when polls closed at 6 p.m. (1600 GMT).

Before leaving Berat, a volley of shots was fired near the helicopters. One Italian pilot had a narrow escape earlier on Sunday when his helicopter was hit by a bullet as he hovered above the ground on the same spot. The bullet entered the bottom of the cockpit and exited through the glass.
No-one was injured and Italian troops on the ground were unable to flush out the gunman.

In the southern town of Gjirokaster near the Greek border, OSCE officials said two men fired shots at ballot boxes inside a polling station in the nearby village of Dervican. The gunmen were apparently related to a guard at the Greek consulate in Gjirokaster who was shot dead on Saturday night.

"He was shot dead because he had apparently seen another killing and was to be a witness," OSCE monitor Hans-Jurg Pfaff of Switzerland told reporters in a field near the town guarded by Romanian soldiers.
He said by 11 a.m., around 50 percent of registered voters had cast their ballot in the Gjirokaster region. Observers would be present at 15 of 400 polling stations in the area.

Lalumiere said she was told by Gjirokaster mayor Ylli Asllani, a Democrat, that members of his party had been able to take their places on electoral commissions despite rumours that they had been threatened.

Giving her overall impression after also hearing reports from observers near the northern towns of Shkoder and Lezhe, and visiting a polling station in the southeastern town of Korce, Lalumiere said voting seemed to have gone relatively smoothly.

"The procedures, from what we have seen and heard, were satisfactory and the turnout very good, up to 80 percent in some areas," said Lalumiere, a former Council of Europe secretary-general. "I was glad to hear there had been no intimidation of commission members in Gjirokaster."

Apart from Lushnje, the mood was generally calm and relaxed, which belied the violence and chaos that has gripped Albania since unrest erupted in March after thousands lost their cash in collapsed pyramid investment schemes.

Observers in all the towns visited said that apart from minor incidents, such as a handful of names missing off electoral registers, election procedures were generally respected, but voters were apprehensive about what would happen when the results were announced.
"Many people are frightened about what will happen in the next day or two," an OSCE official in Gjirokaster said.
